Shaking of the bea{{ls}}t.''] The promes of Chri{{ls}}t ''(Marc. 16'') that venemous {{ls}}erpents {{ls}}hould not hurt them that beleeue in him, is fulfilled not in al beleuers, but in {{ls}}uch as had the gift of miracles, as S. Paul had. Vvhom here a viper by nature {{ls}}o venemous that the people thought he {{ls}}hould haue died out of hand, did no vvhit annoy: he extingui{{ls}}hing by the povver of Chri{{ls}}t al the poi{{ls}}on of the bea{{ls}}t. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Malta hath S. Paules praiers the Iland vvas deliuered for euer from al {{ls}}uch venemous {{ls}}erpents, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''4 Reg. 2, 19''.}}in {{ls}}o much that children there play vvith {{ls}}corpions euer {{ls}}ince that time, and Pilgrimes daily carie vvith them peeces of {{ls}}tones out of the place vvhete S. Paul abode, by vvhich they affirme that they heale them vvhich in other countries adioyning are bitten of {{ls}}corpions, the medicine therfore being called, ''S. Paules grace''. The Heretikes that knovv not the povver of God, nor {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Gods miraculous vertue in certaine countries and creatures, by his Saincts.}}the miraculous vertues giuen to his Saincts, maruel and bla{{ls}}pheme, vvhen they heare {{ls}}uch things as be proper to certaine countries, attributed {{ls}}ometimes to Gods miracles done by his Saincts: as though that vvere not po{{ls}}sible, or vvere not as much to Gods honour, and more, then things proceding only of natural cau{{ls}}es. Such profane men vvould not haue attributed the hol{{ls}}omnes of the vvaters of Iericho to Eli{{ls}}eus his vertue and miracles, amending them by ca{{ls}}ting {{ls}}alt into them, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Tho. Fazellus de rebus Siculis decad. 1 li. 1 c. 1''.}}if the Scripture had not expre{{ls}}ly te{{ls}}tified the {{ls}}ame. It is the part of al faithful men to referre {{ls}}uch things to God, vvhen any iu{{ls}}t occa{{ls}}ion is giuen thereunto, rather then to nature: though the incredulous doe alvvaies contrarie, for feare of {{ls}}uper{{ls}}tition & di{{ls}}honouring God. As though this e{{ls}}cape of drovvning, might better and more to Gods glorie be referred to chaunce and the mariners indu{{ls}}trie, then to S. Paules praiers and extraordinarie vvorking.
